candidates.title: Find local news gaps across outlets

demandEvidence.chore: Compare operator-supplied coverage summaries from selected foreign and local outlets to flag topics not represented locally.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Building a tool to see what is yet not picked up by the outlets in your own country.

experimentPlan.output: A short list of topics present in supplied foreign-outlet summaries but absent from supplied local-outlet summaries.
inputs: Three to ten fictional article headlines with outlet and date.
A small operator-selected list of local outlets and topic labels.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies one fixed batch of headlines and outlet labels.
steps: Normalize headlines into short topic descriptions.
Group likely matching topics for human review.
Compare topic groups with the supplied local outlet list.
Return only candidate gaps with the source headlines attached.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a synthetic batch with known overlapping topics, verify every flagged gap is absent from the local list and every known overlap is not flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An editor must select lawful sources and verify coverage; the tool must not present an absence as fact without checking the actual outlet archive.
unverified: Reliable outlet data access and coverage completeness.
Topic matching quality across different headlines.
Whether newsroom buyers want or would pay for this output.

ease.reason: A beginner could compare a few operator-supplied article summaries, but no source documents a collection or comparison method.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: local newsrooms or media researchers might pay for a coverage-gap brief; this maker post does not establish buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week manual-input prototype is bounded, but outlet selection, topic matching and reliable coverage remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable comparison could flag candidate gaps; a person must choose sources and verify every finding before use.

evidence.reason: The post states a tool idea about stories not picked up locally, but gives no workflow detail, examples or corroborated need.

candidates.reason: Freshly assessed scoped experiment; provisional mean is below 6 and remains rejected.

candidates.title: Flag repeat processing after missed triggers

demandEvidence.chore: Detect a repeated batch or record after a missed schedule trigger before the operator processes it again.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.

experimentPlan.output: A review list of synthetic lead records that appear to belong to an already processed batch.
inputs: Fictional lead rows with operator-chosen stable IDs.
A fictional log of previously processed batch IDs.
A proposed duplicate rule supplied by the operator.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a new fictional batch alongside its processed-ID log.
steps: Compare each row ID with the supplied processed IDs.
Group exact matches and preserve the matching IDs.
Mark nonmatches as unreviewed rather than safe to process.
Produce a report for an operator to inspect.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Test known repeated and new IDs; the report must flag every known repeat, retain its matching ID, and never claim a nonmatch is safe without the operator’s rule.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A workflow operator supplies stable identifiers and decides whether to skip, investigate or replay any batch; no live trigger or data connection is proposed.
unverified: The actual duplicate key and recovery policy.
Whether missed triggers recur in the operator’s workflow.
Any safe integration with the schedule or lead system.

ease.reason: A beginner can create a small synthetic duplicate check, but no supplied implementation reference documents scheduler recovery or idempotency.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Shopify lead-generation operators may pay to prevent duplicate processing; this post gives no purchase or payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare fictional batch identifiers, while safe replay and the workflow’s actual duplicate key are unknown.

autonomy.reason: A proposed checker can flag matching identifiers, but a person must decide whether to skip or replay work.

evidence.reason: The retained task span explicitly says missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything, but does not specify frequency, records or recovery rules.

candidates.reason: Freshly assessed scoped experiment; provisional mean is below 6 and remains rejected.

candidates.title: Review received images with customer messages

demandEvidence.chore: Use an already received customer image together with its text message to prepare a product-identification draft, without asking the customer to resend the image.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want the AI agent to recognize that the image has already been received and use the available image to identify the product

experimentPlan.output: A draft product-identification question or candidate based on a supplied message and its already attached test image.
inputs: A synthetic product image with a known label.
A proposed catalog excerpt supplied by the operator.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one paired message and image fixture.
steps: Keep the text and image attached to the same test case.
Compare visible image details with the supplied catalog excerpt.
Draft a candidate product match with uncertainty noted.
Hold the result for human review; do not contact the customer.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Run paired-image, text-only and mismatched-image fixtures; confirm the draft references only the attached fixture and flags uncertain or absent matches for review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator must provide authorized test images and catalog data, verify the match and approve any customer response; the prototype sends nothing.
unverified: Whether Make can pass the downloaded image to the same agent input.
Image-analysis accuracy for the shop’s products.
Catalog and Messenger access, permissions and retention rules.

ease.reason: A paired text-and-image mock is possible, but no supplied building reference documents Make file transfer or image interpretation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online shops might pay to reduce repeated image requests; the discussion proves no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can test fictional paired inputs, while connector mapping, image access and product accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed draft can combine supplied text and image descriptions; a person must verify the product and send any reply.

evidence.reason: The full retained post describes the message, downloaded image and resend problem, but offers no corroborated demand or implementation reference.

candidates.reason: Freshly assessed scoped experiment; provisional mean is below 6 and remains rejected.

candidates.title: Review repeated Make data-sync failures

demandEvidence.chore: Review a supplied example of duplicate records created during a data sync and prepare an operator-facing failure summary.

experimentPlan.output: A review card describing a supplied Make scenario error and the operator’s next diagnostic question.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one synthetic failure example for review.
steps: Capture the supplied module and error text.
Compare the actual result with the operator’s expected result.
Draft a concise discrepancy summary and one question for diagnosis.
If the scenario reports a module error, route it to the configured Make error handler for operator review.
Hold all suggested changes for an operator.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic error and non-error examples, verify that the card preserves the supplied message, identifies the expected-versus-actual difference and never asserts an unobserved root cause.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies safe test text, reviews the card and configures any Make error route; the reference does not establish prevention of duplicate records or automatic fixes.
unverified: Whether the reported sync issue creates a Make module error that the handler can intercept.
How duplicate records are identified and repaired.
Whether operators experience this often or would pay for help.

ease.reason: A beginner can test a small error summary; the Make reference documents an error route that intercepts module errors, not duplicate detection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional automation consultants may pay for a repeatable fault-review service; this offer establishes no paying customers.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic failure-summary mock is bounded, but the reference does not cover record matching or the listed integrations.

autonomy.reason: A supplied error can be turned into a review card; the Make reference supports an error route, while a person must diagnose and fix the cause.

evidence.reason: The retained post lists recurring sync examples including duplicate records, but no particular incident, frequency or buyer need is verified.
